root_cause: The modal's focus trap does not handle shift+tab wrapping from the first focusable element to the last; instead, focus leaves the modal and is returned to the modal container due to the focusin listener, causing focus to land on the modal element (tabindex="-1") rather than wrapping.
repair_strategy: Add Tab and Shift+Tab keydown listener to the modal that prevents default and moves focus to the opposite end of the focusable elements when at boundaries, implementing a circular focus trap.
expected_accessibility_effect: Shift+Tab from the first focusable element (close button) will now move focus to the last focusable element (delete button), satisfying the requirement that backward navigation wraps within the modal.
functional_risks: Custom keyboard handlers in modal content may interfere with the added Tab listener.
If the modal contains no focusable elements, focus wrapping may not work as expected.
The focusable element selector may not match all focusable cases (e.g., elements with tabindex>=0 or contenteditable), leading to incorrect wrapping.
Potential performance impact from querying focusable elements on each keydown (negligible).
verification_requirements: Verify that Tab moves focus forward through all focusable elements and wraps from last to first.
Verify that Shift+Tab moves focus backward and wraps from first to last.
Ensure Escape key still closes the modal.
Ensure modal initial focus still works when shown.
Ensure focus is not trapped when modal contains no focusable elements (should fallback to modal itself).
Verify that clicking outside or on backdrop still dismisses the modal as configured.
